title: Density-Dependent Gravitational Coupling Predicts ISW Sign-Flip in Deep Voids
description: Derives how Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), with an effective Poisson coupling µ that increases with density, adds a non-linear Rees–Sciama term to the ISW signal that is positive in voids. This term partially cancels the standard linear ISW cold spot and forces a sign flip (net hot spot) for sufficiently deep voids, with the turnover near δ ≈ −0.7 for typical supervoid scales. The paper provides concrete, depth-binned stacking tests using BOSS/DESI void catalogs and Planck CMB data.

isw_decomposition.description: Time variation of the gravitational potential acquires the standard linear ISW term plus a non-linear term when the effective coupling \mu depends on density.

mu_k_rho.description: EFC effective Poisson coupling; density dependence enters through the stiffness response R(k,\rho) which depends on \Gamma'(\rho).

R_k_rho.description: Stiffness response amplifies at large scales (R \propto k^{-4}); with \Gamma'(\rho) from grid-mode BE statistics, this induces strong low-\rho sensitivity in \mu.

chain_rule.description: Relates time variation of \mu to the local density evolution; in expanding voids d\rho/dt < 0.

rs_term_sign.description: With d\mu/d\rho > 0 and d\rho/dt < 0 in voids, the RS contribution is positive (hot) and opposes the linear ISW cold spot.

Atotal_def.description: Amplitude ratio used to quantify deviation from \LambdaCDM; crosses zero when the net ISW signal flips sign.

scaling_RS_over_ISW.description: Approximate scaling showing RS grows rapidly in deep, low-density voids, driving the turnover and sign flip.

key_results.main_finding: EFC predicts that the void ISW signal flips sign (net hot spot) for deep voids, with A_total crossing zero near δ ≈ −0.7 and becoming strongly negative by δ ≲ −0.8 (e.g., A_total ≈ −0.83 at δ = −0.8).

sealed_predictions.statement: Depth-dependent turnover: stacked void ISW amplitude weakens with increasing |δ_v| and crosses zero for the deepest voids (|δ_v| ≳ 0.7).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Depth-binned void–CMB stacking (Planck SMICA) for BOSS DR12 or DESI shows monotonically increasing |ΔT| with |δ_v| across all bins, with no turnover.

sealed_predictions.statement: Scale dependence: the sign-flip occurs at shallower |δ_v| for larger voids (lower k), due to R(k) ∝ k^{-4}.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Cross-binning by size and depth finds no trend (or the opposite trend) in turnover depth with R_v at ≥2σ.

sealed_predictions.statement: Redshift evolution: the RS/ISW ratio increases toward lower z; the turnover (or sign-flip) occurs at shallower |δ_v| at lower redshift.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Comparing stacks at z ≈ 0.7 vs z ≈ 0.3 shows no shift toward shallower |δ_v| at lower z within uncertainties.

sealed_predictions.statement: Deepest-void sign: for |δ_v| ≳ 0.8 supervoids (R_v ~ 100–150 Mpc), the net stack should be a hot spot (A_total < 0).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Deepest-bin stacks remain cold (A_total ≥ 0) at >3σ across independent surveys (e.g., BOSS DR12, DESI) with validated systematics.

kill_criteria: KC1: Depth-binned void–CMB stacking with Planck SMICA (or equivalent) for BOSS DR12 and/or DESI shows a strictly monotonic increase of |ΔT| with |δ_v| across all bins (no weakening or turnover) at ≥3σ, contradicting the dµ/dρ > 0 prediction.

KC2: In the deepest quartile (|δ_v| ≥ 0.8, R_v ≳ 100 Mpc), the stacked signal remains a cold spot with A_total ≥ 0 at >3σ after thorough null/systematics tests (rotations, randoms, lensing-leakage control) in at least two independent surveys.

KC3: Cross depth×size analysis finds that larger voids require deeper |δ_v| to approach turnover (or show the opposite trend) at ≥2σ, violating the predicted R(k) ∝ k^{-4} scaling that pushes the sign-flip to shallower |δ_v| for larger R_v.
KC4: Redshift-binned analyses (e.g., z ≈ 0.7 vs z ≈ 0.3) detect no increase in RS/ISW ratio toward lower redshift (or observe the opposite trend) at ≥2σ, falsifying the predicted evolution.

KC5: A comprehensive reanalysis attributes any observed turnover to identified systematics (e.g., selection, photometric z-bias, foregrounds), and after correction the stacks revert to ΛCDM-like monotonic behavior across depth and size bins at ≥2σ, removing support for density-dependent µ effects.

abstract: Shows that EFC's density-dependent μ(ρ) produces a non-linear ISW (Rees-Sciama) contribution with opposite sign to the standard linear ISW in cosmic voids. For deep voids (δ ≲ −0.8), the net ISW signal flips sign: a void produces a hot spot instead of the expected cold spot. The sign follows structurally from dμ/dρ > 0 (BE statistics). Testable via depth-binned void-CMB stacking.

predictions.description: Depth-dependent ISW turnover in void-CMB stacking
Scale dependence: sign-flip at shallower |δ| for larger voids
Redshift evolution: RS/ISW ratio increases at lower z
